## What's new

Threadnote 5 gives coding agents a trustworthy context lifecycle: begin non-trivial work with a brief grounded in the
current source, use the checkout as authority, and close with a private handoff plus a reviewable proposal for knowledge
worth keeping. You decide what is saved, shared, corrected, or retired.

Beta 4 makes that lifecycle easier to maintain in established projects. Context Health can now be narrowed to a kind of
knowledge, a topic, or a specific problem such as an unknown citation. Large result sets can be reviewed in stable
pages, and repair previews keep the exact same scope, so a focused cleanup does not quietly expand into unrelated
memories. If the underlying context changes during review, Threadnote asks for a fresh view instead of mixing old and
new evidence.

Connected agents can use this maintenance lifecycle through the standard Threadnote connection. Open Context Health in
Manager or ask the agent to inspect a focused area; review the proposed repairs before approving any change. The same
connection also supports ownership and review-date updates, local recall feedback, and publishing verified procedures,
while actions that change saved knowledge still require an explicit approval step.

Setup remains preview-first and installs concise guidance so agents create Context Briefs and closeout handoffs as part
of normal work. No special prompt is required for those routine lifecycle steps, and no working context is shared
automatically.
